methods.text: Ask a visitor to predict the outcome before showing it, then compare the two.
Change one input at a time and write down everything that moved.
Hand the controls to someone else and stay silent for two minutes.
Explain the project in three captions, then cut the one nobody needs.
Set every control to its extreme and check the result still makes sense.
Play the project as a game with one extra rule, then remove the rule.
Record a short walkthrough and mark each moment of hesitation.
Write the question the visitor arrives with at the top of your notes.
Build a version with one deliberate error and see if testers notice it.
Start from one surprising observation and design toward it.
Run the same scenario three times with different starting values.
Turn one hidden calculation into something the visitor can see.
Describe the screen aloud to someone who cannot see it, then fix what was hard to say.
Give a tester a goal instead of an instruction and watch the route they take.
Keep a list of every guessed number and replace one guess per pass.
End each session by naming one thing a visitor can now try that they could not before.

constraints.text: Every simulation can pause, advance one step and reset.
Every control shows its current value as text.
Random results can be repeated from a visible seed.
Every chart or diagram has a short text summary of what it shows.

tasks.text: Queue simulator: a playground for small cafe owners that changes staff count and arrival rate and shows how the line grows or clears over a busy hour.
Rhythm sketchpad: an instrument for beginner music students that places beats on a loop and lets them hear how shifting one beat changes the groove.
Erosion sandbox: an explorable model for school geography classes that sets rainfall and slope and shows how a riverbank wears away over time.
Heat loss explorer: a tool for renters planning for winter that toggles curtains, draughts and thermostat settings and shows the estimated heat lost from one room.
Signal relay game: a logic puzzle for players who like routing problems that sends messages between stations with delays and shows which ones arrive late.
Fieldnote sorter: a local tool for birdwatching clubs that tags sightings by time and place and shows which hours of the day bring the most variety.

temperaments.text: Answers a question with a quick experiment.
Restates the goal whenever the talk drifts.
Asks for the simplest case before the general one.
Proposes a test that could prove them wrong.
Compares every idea to one from another field.
Holds back until everyone has given a number.
Asks who would use it on their worst day.
Builds a rough version rather than discuss it.

temperaments: Asks what the user can do with it.
Pushes for one more pass on the weakest state.
Shows a working sample before making a claim.
Checks the small screen before agreeing.
Questions every effect with no useful result.
Asks how a person gets back after a mistake.
Notices uneven spacing before anyone else.
methods: List each state before drawing the first frame.
Build the useful action before adding any motion.
Reserve space for the longest label in every state.
Compare the resting state with the state after an error.
Try every action twice before calling it finished.
Work through the whole control without touching a mouse.
Test with a long name and an empty value.
Make the main action clear before adding a hint.
Remove any effect that hides the result.
Give one transition a clear start, middle and end.
Interrupt each transition halfway and keep the state correct.
Check the edge alignment before adding shadows.
Choose one spacing unit and use it throughout.
Draw focus and pressed states beside the resting state.
Show what changes when the main action succeeds.
Make failure easy to spot and easy to recover from.
constraints: Every action works without a mouse.
Tap targets are at least 44 pixels tall.
Text stays legible at 200 percent zoom.
Every action gives immediate visible feedback.
tasks: Feature details: an accordion for a product page that expands one feature and keeps the other summaries easy to scan.
Preview zoom: a slider for an image editor that changes magnification while keeping the selected area in view.
Save notice: a toast for a project editor that confirms a save and then clears without blocking the work.
Item quantity: a stepper for a shopping cart that changes item count and updates the total.
Product rating: a rating control for a shop that lets someone select a score and change it before saving.
Workspace search: a search field for a team app that filters project names and shows when nothing matches.
